chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from al-'Ubaydi from Kharash from Zurarah from one of the Imams (peace be upon him)
Regarding four men who testified against a woman for adultery, and she said, 'I am a virgin,' so the women looked at her and found her to be a virgin, he said, 'The testimony of women is accepted.'
ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of women accepted in cases of adultery in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies that in cases of zina where the accused claims virginity, the testimony of women is accepted based on physical examination (tashkhis) by other women, a ruling derived from the Prophet's practice. It underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence in accepting female testimony in specific, private contexts where male witnesses might be less effective or where the matter is inherently personal. This principle is often cited by scholars like Al-Shirazi and Al-Khoei to support the admissibility of women's testimony in financial and personal status cases under certain conditions.
